nodes.title: How to use / status
widgets_values:
### Mathematador isolated-character pose set

Generates the boy and Toro Numerico (bull) as separate full-body reference PNGs on a plain background (for individual rembg background removal), across a small pose sheet: standing, walking, cool (arms crossed), success (thumbs up), and failure (sad). NOT the two-character interaction scene (that is mathematador-video.json, still unresolved due to AnimateDiff ghosting/occlusion).

Status as of 2026-09-28:
- Boy: all 5 poses confirmed (seed 7001, fixed). Standing/walk/cool/success/failure all match the approved design and intended gesture/expression.
- Bull: 4 of 5 poses confirmed (seed 7006, fixed). Standing/walk/cool/success confirmed. Failure/sad pose could not be achieved reliably -- the approved base description contains the literal phrase warm smile as a core trait, which fights any sad-expression prompt. Removing that phrase, adding strong negative weighting against smiling/cheerful, and raising cfg to 8.5 still produced a smiling bull. A reliable fix would need pose/expression guidance (e.g. ControlNet), not more prompt tuning -- logged here so this is not re-attempted blindly. Not included in this workflow.

Critical technique lesson learned this session: when adding a pose/expression variant to an already-approved character, do NOT shorten, reorder, or rewrite the approved base description -- SDXL's CLIP encoder has a ~75-token attention window, and rewriting/compacting the prompt causes real design drift (confirmed: one attempt reverted the bipedal cartoon bull to a plain four-legged animal; another gave it a bodybuilder physique; a boy attempt added an unintended hat and changed hair color). The reliable pattern is: prepend the pose/expression phrase in front of the UNCHANGED, VERBATIM approved base text (single character full body reference, {pose}, {exact approved text}), and put any anatomy/style fixes in the NEGATIVE prompt only, never as new positive descriptors, to avoid drifting the established look.

Note: seed's control_after_generate is set to fixed on every KSampler so re-running reproduces the same result -- change to randomize for variations.

See mathematador-app/assets/working/comfy-workflows/README.md for the fuller project history.
